claims.text: 2023 annual real GDP growth was 2.5 percent, which is a year-over-year increase from the 2022 annual level to the 2023 annual level, whereas quarterly figures like the 3.3 percent Q4 2023 rate are annualized quarter-over-quarter rates rather than full-year growth.

citations.quotation: Real GDP increased 2.5 percent in 2023 (from the 2022 annual level to the 2023 annual level), compared with an increase of 1.9 percent in 2022 (table 1).
Real gross domestic product (GDP) increased at an annual rate of 3.3 percent in the fourth quarter of 2023

claims.text: The annual (2.5%) and quarterly annualized (3.3% in Q4, 4.9% in Q3) figures measure different things: annual growth compares full calendar-year levels, while quarterly annualized rates extrapolate a single quarter's change to a full-year pace, so they can differ substantially.

citations.quotation: In the third quarter, real GDP increased 4.9 percent.

counterarguments.text: The 2.5 percent figure comes from the advance estimate, which is based on incomplete data and subject to revision, so the final annual growth rate could differ.

citations.quotation: The GDP estimate released today is based on source data that are incomplete or subject to further revision by the source agency

limitations: No explanation of the quarterly annualization methodology is provided in the sources; the distinction between annual and annualized quarterly rates is inferred from standard conventions.
The figures are advance estimates and may be revised.
